title: Marginal rates rise with income; brackets explained, not advised

steps.reply: Tax brackets are marginal — only the dollars inside each bracket get that rate. If you're in the 22% bracket, your first dollars are still taxed at 10% and 12%. Your effective rate (total tax ÷ total income) is always lower than your bracket. The OBBBA made the seven TCJA brackets permanent, inflation-adjusted for 2026.

title: Gig worker: irregular income and quarterly tax facts

steps.reply: Self-employment tax is 15.3% — 12.4% Social Security up to the $184,500 wage base plus 2.9% Medicare (no cap) — on top of income tax, applied to 92.35% of net earnings. Gig platforms don't withhold: track mileage and expenses from day one, set aside 25–30% of every payout immediately, and make quarterly estimated payments.
